summary: A 1933 tower with an L-4 cab replaced a 1920s platform on Huckleberry Mountain; sources disagree on its height and on whether it fell in 1974 or 1976.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a native timber tower
facts.status_note: The tower is gone. Sources give 1974 or 1976 as the year it came down.

events.note: A platform was constructed in the 1920s
Tower with an L-4 cab; a CCC crew erected the timber tower that fall
Earliest lookout named in the sources; the 1921 newspaper item mentions the summit lookout
Timber fire between Whitney and Sumpter, sighted by the lookout; 80 acres of timber destroyed
Lightning fire of about a third of an acre, spotted from the lookout
Forest Service inspection on November 27 (memo dated November 30, 1967); repairs estimated to give at most five more years
Last name on the firelookout.com list; not necessarily the final season
Register says the lookout was destroyed in 1974
Forest Lookouts page dates the destruction to 1976; conflicts with 1974

corrections.why: 4.3 m is about 14 ft, which matches the 14 x 14 ft cab rather than the tower. The 1933 newspaper and the 1967 memo give 20 ft (6.1 m); the register and firelookout.com give 22 ft (6.7 m). Sources disagree, so 6.1 m is the contemporary figure, not a settled one.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1920s platform is a separate structure; all three sources date the tower with the L-4 cab to 1933.

sources.title: Huckleberry Mountain Lookout Site (Baker County), Former Fire Lookout Sites Register

notes_for_editor: Record height 4.3 m matches the 14 ft cab width, not the tower; corrected to a range. Height (20 vs 22 ft) and fate year (1974 vs 1976) are unresolved. The 1920 built year is the 1920s platform, not the tower. The 1946 survey disk is a possible remnant, but nothing says it survives. WebSearch returned other Huckleberry Mountain lookouts (Wyoming, Lewis County WA, Prospect OR), which were excluded. No source describes the site or access today.
